Project Page | Paper | GitHub

	
		
		Overview
	

AutoElicit-Bench is a benchmark of 117 human-verified perturbations for evaluating the robustness of Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) against unintended behaviors. These perturbations were successfully elicited from Claude 4.5 Haiku (50) and Claude 4.5 Opus (67) using the AutoElicit framework.
Each perturbation is a minimally modified, realistic instruction derived from OSWorld tasks that can trigger unsafe behaviors… See the full description on the dataset page: https://huggingface.co/datasets/osunlp/AutoElicit-Bench.
evaluation_method: task_success_rate (measured as safety_violation_rate / fraction of perturbations that elicit unsafe/unintended behavior), typically verified by human annotation
general_score_metric: safety_violation_rate (percentage of perturbations that successfully elicit unsafe behavior)
reputation: A focused, emerging safety benchmark (hosted on Hugging Face) used for evaluating adversarial elicitation of unsafe behaviors in instruction-following agents.
